decisions.question: The 2 % rule's own limits in D: a core sandwiched between cheeks that crosses 2 % (§17.2 'Design question for M3'), plus a sealed cavity, flush layers and sheets (§17.2 'What the 2 % rule itself admits'). How should a cleaned part affect Thinness' chords?
decisions.default: Option 0: cleaned parts are inert in every factor. A cleaned part is in no work set, so Thinness' chord through it stays open, and chords merge gaps up to CONTACT_TOL as §5.2 says. The class is documented with the measured sweep.
decisions.evidence: Measured on the snapshot through the emulator, rank order, with the build's own verdict. 9 sandwiches, core kept against the same design hollow: 6 tier flips on 4 designs, largest |ΔD| 0.3235 (LAM1). In LAM1, SurfaceComplexity carries +0.2876 of Hammering's +0.3235 and Thinness only +0.0359; SC carries all of Sharpening's +0.2000; Volume moves Smelting −0.0520. The rule's other limits: a closed box gives Smelting 0.1376 → 0.4463; 8 flush layers give Hammering 0.0582 → 0.7000; 14 sheets give |ΔD| 0.3639. No M3-side rule reaches any of these. Option B is unchecked: it would edit M2's measure, and its old numbers (5 flips against 6, up to +23 % cost) came from the prototype's verdict.

decisions.question: T-DIF-07(b), flush re-segmentation: assert §14.6's tolerances on general designs (Gen.segmented), or narrow the contract?
decisions.default: (i) Keep §5.2's stride, walked in measureRanked order. Assert (b) on E-S2.10's F5 cuts (2, 3 and 7 pieces) and on C12 against C02. On Gen.segmented, assert Volume and EdgeLength and only report Thinness, Asymmetry, SurfaceComplexity and G. Record the sensitivity in §5.6 and §17.2. A redesign (ii) is a separate study.

On 300 Gen designs (TestRng 0x5EED0007) with the stride: Thinness 0.0591 (#51), Asymmetry 0.0197 (#152), SC 0.0056, G 0.0236, 0 tier flips; Volume and EdgeLength 0. summary:
I wrote plan-r2.md (115 KB), a complete M3 plan that stands without plan.md, and put every script its numbers depend on, with their outputs, in proto-r2/.

All numbers were re-measured on my own copy of the m2x-r4-base snapshot, through M2's emulator of M3 running on the build's exact verdict.

- **§5.5 and E-S2.9:** in part order the emulator reproduces both exactly, character for character on E-S2.9's 80 rows.
- **Rank order (§17.2):** walking Sampling.measureRanked changes §5.5 in one cell, C09's Hammering 0.3170 → 0.3186, and E-S2.9's C09 Thinness All 0.3858 → 0.3898.
- **Order dependence:** in part order, C09's 300 permutations give Hammering 0.3170–0.3195 and P5's 60 give 0.1853–0.1902, as §17.2 says. In rank order every fixture gives one bit-identical outcome, edge and grip point included.
- **Contracts and invariances:**
  - T-DIF-04 is bit-identical on every case, including 100 Gen designs per filler kind.
  - T-DIF-06, T-DIF-13 and the T-EDG items reproduce, and the EdgeLength cap case measures 8.2001.
  - Translation passes T-DIF-07(a).
  - Flush re-segmentation fails on general designs to the critique's digits (G 0.0236, still 0.0191 with every sample a probe), but passes exactly on E-S2.10's cuts.
- **Time budget (quiet machine, median of 15):**
  - The verdict alone takes at most 29.1 ms and M2's phases at most 35.4 ms.
  - With M3 emulated, the slowest valid design takes 48.99 ms Lune, 11 ms under the 60 ms guard, and every gap stays ≤ 0.317 ms.
  - --quick takes 16.94 s and the full suite 168.88 s.
- **Decisions:**
  - D1 stays option 0 **[Decision to confirm]** (O10): no M3-side rule reaches the sandwich, sealed cavity, flush layers or sheets; SurfaceComplexity and Volume carry the jump, not Thinness.
  - D2 stays (i) **[Decision to confirm]** (O11).
  - D3 is settled at CHECK_UNITS 500, with finer M3 charges.
  - D4–D6 stand as in plan.md.
  - New D7 updates O7's figure to include M3.
- **The rest of the plan:**
  - the snapshot interface, checked;
  - the module APIs;
  - fixtures with literal rows and margins;
  - test definitions;
  - the order of work for 4 sequential builders;
  - the SPEC edits;
  - risks;
  - critique.md's points as they stand now;
  - an anchor index and a measurement index.
